papers.title: Paediatric Helicobacter pylori infection and allergic and inflammatory diseases: a contemporary systematic review with meta-analysis
papers.authors: Tavares M, Ferreira A, Campo E, Santos Silva E, Lima R, Lopes A
papers.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is prevalent worldwide, and its potential protective role in allergic and immune diseases has been a topic of speculation. This systematic review aims to analyse recent literature to establish a consensus on this relationship. Articles published in the past 12 years regarding association of H. pylori and various allergic diseases were screened. Thirty-five articles from three databases were assessed for bias using the ROBINS-E tool. Objective data from each article were collected for this review. Among the reviewed articles, 14 focused on asthma, 10 on eliac disease(CeD), 5 on eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), 7 on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and 8 on mixed conditions. In the asthma meta-analysis, H. pylori infection was not significantly associated with asthma overall (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.54-1.05; I2 = 67.3%). Subgroup analyses showed an inverse association in studies using UBT/SAT, whereas histology-based studies showed no association. Low-risk-of-bias studies likewise showed no significant association. Results for celiac and IBD were mixed. No clear trends were observed for the other conditions analysed.
CONCLUSION: Current paediatric evidence does not demonstrate a significant overall association between H. pylori infection and asthma. Apparent inverse associations were confined to specific diagnostic and risk-of-bias subgroups. Evidence for celiac disease, IBD, EoE, and other immune-mediated disorders remains inconsistent. More prospective paediatric studies are needed to understand the immune modulation of H. pylori infection.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • The relationship between Helicobacter pylori infection and allergic or immune-mediated diseases remains complex and incompletely understood. • Previous studies, including mixed studies with adult and paediatric populations, have reported inconsistent and sometimes conflicting associations.
WHAT IS NEW: • This is the first comprehensive paediatric review covering multiple conditions simultaneously, synthesising evidence on the association between Helicobacter pylori infection and allergic and immune-mediated diseases. • Analysis of paediatric data found no overall association between H. pylori infection and asthma risk. Histology-based studies confirmed this finding, whereas a slight inverse association was observed only in studies using non-invasive diagnostic methods (UBT or SAT) and in those with a higher risk of bias.

papers.title: Modified LIFT via a Lateral Approach Versus Standard LIFT for Transsphincteric Anal Fistula: A Prospective Randomized Study
papers.abstract:
AIM: To compare the early clinical outcomes of modified ligation of the intersphincteric fistula tract (LIFT) via a lateral approach with those of standard LIFT in patients with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed transsphincteric anal fistula.
METHODS: This single-center prospective randomized study included adult patients with transsphincteric anal fistula who were treated between January and May 2024 and were followed through August 2024. Among 96 patients assessed for eligibility, 46 met the eligibility criteria, and 40 consenting patients were randomized at a 1:1 ratio to standard LIFT or modified LIFT via a lateral approach. Follow-up was performed at postoperative weeks 1, 4, 8, and 12. The primary outcome was wound healing time. Secondary outcomes included early recurrence or persistence, postoperative pain assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS), and continence evaluated using the Cleveland Clinic Fecal Incontinence Scale.
RESULTS: A total of 40 patients were analyzed, with 20 patients in each group. Baseline demographic and available clinical characteristics were comparable between the groups. The median wound healing time was significantly shorter in the modified LIFT group than in the standard LIFT group (13 [interquartile range, 10-17] days vs. 29.5 [26-32] days; p < 0.001). No early recurrence or persistence was observed in the modified LIFT group by week 12. In the standard LIFT group, recurrence/persistence was observed in 3 of the 20 patients (15.0%) at week 8 and in 6 of the 20 patients (30.0%) at week 12 (Fisher exact test at week 12; p = 0.020). The median VAS pain scores were low and comparable in the standard LIFT versus modified LIFT groups at week 1 (0.90 vs. 0.95; p = 0.942) and week 4 (0.00 vs. 0.00; p = 0.115). No case of fecal incontinence was noted in either group during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with transsphincteric anal fistula, compared with standard LIFT, modified LIFT via a lateral approach was associated with faster early wound healing and a lower rate of early recurrence/persistence within 12 weeks, without an observed increase in postoperative pain or fecal incontinence. Larger studies with longer follow-up are warranted before definitive conclusions can be drawn regarding long-term recurrence.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07603635.

papers.title: Pfannenstiel versus periumbilical specimen extraction in laparoscopic low anterior resection: a comparative analysis of incisional hernia risk, postoperative recovery, and oncologic outcomes
papers.authors: Kang S, Shin D, Bae H, Han Y, Cho M, Hur H
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incisional hernia is a common long-term complication following colorectal surgery. In laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, specimen extraction is most commonly performed via a periumbilical midline incision, although the Pfannenstiel incision has emerged as an alternative approach with the potential to reduce hernia rates. However, its adoption has been limited by technical demands, and comparative evidence in a homogeneous rectal cancer cohort remains scarce. This study compared incisional hernia risk, postoperative recovery, and oncologic outcomes according to extraction site in laparoscopic LAR.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent laparoscopic LAR for rectal cancer between 2014 and 2021. Specimen extraction was performed via either a Pfannenstiel incision or a periumbilical midline incision. The primary outcome was incisional hernia at the extraction site, assessed by computed tomography. Secondary outcomes included postoperative recovery, perioperative complications, and long-term oncologic outcomes. Risk factors for incisional hernia were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: Among 242 patients, 115 underwent Pfannenstiel extraction and 127 periumbilical extraction. Incisional hernia occurred in one patient (0.9%) in the Pfannenstiel group and 12 patients (9.4%) in the periumbilical group (p = 0.003). Pfannenstiel extraction was associated with shorter hospital stay, earlier return of bowel function, and lower analgesic requirements. On multivariable analysis, periumbilical extraction was an independent risk factor for incisional hernia. Disease-free and overall survival were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Pfannenstiel specimen extraction was associated with a lower risk of incisional hernia and improved postoperative recovery after laparoscopic LAR without compromising oncologic outcomes, supporting its use as an effective specimen retrieval option in minimally invasive rectal cancer surgery.

papers.title: Patient-, endoscopist-, and procedure-related factors associated with adenoma detection in first screening colonoscopies at a Lebanese tertiary hospital: a retrospective cohort study
papers.authors: Ghantous M, Zayour N, Al Sabagh N, Mchawrab N, Kattan O, Eljammal O
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, and is largely preventable through colonoscopy, during which adenomatous polyps can be detected and removed. The adenoma detection rate (ADR) and polyp detection rate (PDR) are key quality indicators of colonoscopy quality and are inversely associated with post-colonoscopy CRC. These indicators may be influenced by patient-, physician-, and procedure-related factors. This study aimed to evaluate the ADR and PDR, identify factors influencing these indicators, and compare them among gastroenterologists at a Lebanese medical center.
METHODS: This observational, single-center, retrospective cohort study included 257 patients aged 50-75 years who underwent first-time screening colonoscopy over 3 years. Data on patient characteristics and colonoscopy findings were collected. ADR and PDR were calculated according to established guidelines, with ADR additionally estimated using the adenoma-to-polyp detection rate quotient (APDRQ). Descriptive statistics were applied, and chi-square or Fisher's exact tests were used to assess associations between patient-, physician-, and procedural related factors and adenoma detection.
RESULTS: Out of 257 patients, 159 had polyps detected during colonoscopy. The overall ADR was 44.4%, and the PDR was 61.8% over the three-year study period. The ADR was 52.1% in men and 38.0% in women, whereas the PDR was 68.6% in men and 56.3% in women. Although the overall ADR and PDR met or exceeded the recommended benchmarks, disparities were noted in detection rates between males and females. Bowel preparation quality and guarantor type significantly influenced adenoma detection, whereas other factors related to patients and endoscopists had no significant effect. The estimated ADRs derived from the PDRs for five endoscopists were also high, surpassing the 25% benchmark; however, their annual estimated ADRs were relatively below this threshold.
CONCLUSION: This study provides valuable regional data and underscores the need for standardized quality monitoring and further multicentric prospective research to optimize CRC prevention in Lebanon.

papers.title: Safety profile of IL-23 inhibitors from the perspective of physicians and pharmacists: A retrospective real-world pharmacovigilance observational study based on the FAERS database
papers.authors: Guo C, Geng T, Ye L, Sun Z, Zhao S
papers.abstract: ObjectiveInterleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitors are widely used for psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease, yet their long-term safety profiles require continual monitoring. This retrospective observational real-world study aimed to detect potential disproportionate reporting signals associated with tildrakizumab, risankizumab, and guselkumab using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).MethodsAE reports for tildrakizumab, risankizumab, and guselkumab from Q3 2017 to Q3 2025 were retrieved from FAERS. Disproportionality analysis using reporting odds ratios (RORs) was performed, and reported adverse events were classified by system organ classes (SOCs).ResultsA total of 1124, 8574, and 14597 AEs were retrieved for the three IL-23 inhibitors, generating 42, 286, and 348 disproportionate reporting signals, and accumulating 23, 24, and 24 SOCs. Frequently reported AEs included drug ineffectiveness, psoriasis, injection-site reactions, and infections. Disproportionate reporting signals not listed in the current FDA-approved product label comprised cardiovascular events (e.g., myocardial infarction; tildrakizumab ROR = 6.45), malignancies (e.g., malignant melanoma; risankizumab ROR = 8.57), hepatobiliary disorders, and renal complications.ConclusionThese exploratory, hypothesis-generating disproportionate reporting signals may inform routine pharmacovigilance practice for IL-23 inhibitors, alongside well-established common reported events such as infections and systemic reactions. Further pharmacoepidemiologic studies are needed to validate these observations.

papers.title: PDE4DIP/Myomegalin as a Golgi-Centrosome Scaffold in Compartmentalized Signaling, Microtubule Organization, and Disease-Associated Pathway Remodeling
papers.authors: Wang C, Bian C, Wang Z, Luo T
papers.abstract: PDE4DIP/Myomegalin was originally identified as a Golgi- and centrosome-associated protein that interacts with phosphodiesterase 4D, but subsequent work has placed it within a broader network of organelle-associated signaling and cytoskeletal regulation. This review examines PDE4DIP/Myomegalin as a coiled-coil-rich scaffold linking compartmentalized cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)/protein kinase A (PKA) signaling, Golgi-centrosome organization, microtubule architecture, and disease-associated pathway remodeling. At the centrosome, long PDE4D-binding myomegalin forms retain PDE4D3 and restrict local PKA activity, thereby influencing Hedgehog signaling. At the Golgi, AKAP9/AKAP450 provides a major scaffold, while selected myomegalin forms support Golgi-derived microtubule organization and endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi trafficking. In KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer models, PDE4DIP promotes tumor growth and MEK inhibitor resistance through Golgi-associated NF1/RAS pathway remodeling. In non-small cell lung cancer, PDE4DIP cooperates with AKAP9 to maintain Golgi localization and stability of PKA regulatory subunit II alpha; PDE4DIP loss activates PKA/cAMP response element-binding protein signaling and suppresses tumor growth. Cardiovascular studies link myomegalin isoform 4 to sarcomeric PKA signaling, co-occurring PDE4DIP and DES variants to conduction phenotypes, and PDE4DIP dysregulation to left ventricular noncompaction-associated cellular changes, although the evidence remains context dependent. Neurological and retinal disease associations remain largely exploratory. Recent work links a PDE4DIP-AKAP9 interaction to cytoskeletal integrity and RAS-ERK/AKT signaling in podocyte injury. Overall, PDE4DIP/Myomegalin is best understood as an organelle-associated organizer whose effects depend on the experimentally reported form, binding partners, and subcellular address rather than on a single linear pathway.

papers.title: Breaking the Black Box: Revolutionizing Traditional Chinese Medicine with Formula-Derived Nanoparticles
papers.authors: Cheng M, Wen P, Jiang L, Shen H, Wang H
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas produce distinctive multi‑target synergistic therapeutic effects governed by the monarch, minister, assistant, and guide compatibility principle for diverse chronic and refractory disorders. Nevertheless, a four‑layer "black‑box" barrier-encompassing poorly characterized bioactive constituents, ambiguous inter‑component synergistic mechanisms, untraceable in vivo transport profiles, and low oral bioavailability-substantially hinders TCM modernization and global adoption. Most existing reviews focus on single‑component nanocarriers or plant‑derived extracellular‑vesicle‑like particles; few comprehensively investigate nanoparticles generated from complete multi‑herb TCM decoctions while integrating material characterization, mechanistic dissection, and clinical‑regulatory translational bottlenecks. This review addresses this literature gap by focusing on formula‑derived nanoparticles (FDNs), fabricated from intact TCM‑decoction extracts via natural self‑assembly or degradable exogenous carrier‑assisted assembly. FDNs largely retain native component ratios and synergistic bioactivities while enabling precise targeted delivery of herbal constituents. We summarize three mainstream FDN fabrication workflows and establish a comprehensive multidimensional characterization toolkit for assessing physicochemical properties, intermolecular interactions, structural stability, and biocompatibility. Enabled by three quantifiable technical approaches, FDNs can partially mitigate the TCM black‑box dilemma and exert multitarget, precision‑guided intervention against tumors, inflammatory bowel disease, neurodegenerative conditions, and metabolic disorders. Major translational obstacles include non‑standardized industrial scale‑up, insufficient biological barrier penetration, poorly defined molecular interaction mechanisms, absence of unified multicomponent quality benchmarks, incomplete global regulatory frameworks, high manufacturing costs, and risks of poor batch‑to‑batch reproducibility. Priority future directions cover intelligent biomimetic carriers, multiomics‑supported molecular simulation, and end‑to‑end standardized clinical translation, advancing empirical TCM‑formula therapeutics toward standardized, quantifiable high‑precision modern medicine. This review outlines actionable research gaps and a phased translational roadmap to guide investigations.

papers.title: Impact of inflammatory bowel disease on perioperative complications in patients undergoing hysterectomy
papers.authors: Liu H, Chen L, Huang N, Wang Z, Xie H, Chen M
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The global prevalence of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is escalating rapidly, with its associated systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation potentially compromising surgical outcomes. Nevertheless, IBD's influence on perioperative complications following hysterectomy remains unreported. This investigation sought to examine the relationship between IBD and perioperative complications in hysterectomy patients utilizing the National Inpatient Sample database while analyzing associated risk factors.
METHODS: Data for patients who underwent hysterectomy between 2016 and 2022 were obtained from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification codes. Patients younger than 18 years were excluded. Patients were stratified according to the presence or absence of IBD, and demographic characteristics, hospital characteristics, comorbidities, and perioperative outcomes were compared between groups. Statistical analyses included Pearson's χ² test, Wilcoxon rank-sum test, and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 187,401 hysterectomy patients, 853 (0.46%) had comorbid IBD. The prevalence of IBD increased from 0.40% in 2016 to 0.51% in 2022. After multivariable adjustment, IBD was associated with higher odds of sepsis (OR = 3.060; 95% CI = 2.095-4.470), shock (OR = 3.031; 95% CI = 1.605-3.722), acute kidney injury (AKI) (OR = 1.643; 95% CI = 1.235-2.184), urinary tract infection (UTI) (OR = 1.882; 95% CI = 1.332-2.659), and in-hospital mortality (OR = 3.827; 95% CI = 1.855-7.893).
CONCLUSIONS: IBD prevalence among hysterectomy patients increased over time. IBD was associated with higher odds of selected perioperative outcomes, including sepsis, shock, AKI, UTI, and in-hospital mortality. These associations should be interpreted cautiously given the retrospective administrative database design.

papers.title: An ensemble machine learning approach for predicting colorectal polyps using novel inflammatory markers
papers.authors: Zhang L, Wu Y, Jin Q, Wen Y, Wang Y, Qi H
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the associations of two novel inflammatory-nutritional markers, the C-reactive Protein-Albumin-Lymphocyte (CALLY) index and C-reactive protein-to-lymphocyte ratio (CLR), with colorectal polyps, and to develop machine learning models for improved risk prediction.
METHODS: The study conducted a retrospective analysis of 946 patients who underwent colonoscopy at the Second Qilu Hospital of Shandong University from 2023 to 2024. Clinical, laboratory, and endoscopic data were retrieved. Four machine learning models were developed: Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). Additionally, a Stacking ensemble model was constructed, integrating RF, XGBoost, and SVM with logistic regression as the meta-learner. Model performance was evaluated using metrics including the Area Under the Curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Kappa coefficient.
RESULTS: Both the CALLY index and CLR were significantly associated with the presence of colorectal polyps. The Stacking ensemble model achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC: 0.96), outperforming all individual base models. The RF, SVM, and XGBoost models also attained robust predictive capability (AUC: 0.75-0.76). By comparison, LightGBM exhibited suboptimal performance (AUC = 0.72). Feature importance analysis revealed CA19-9 as the top predictive factor.
CONCLUSION: Elevated CLR and reduced CALLY index, together with traditional risk factors, synergistically contribute to colorectal polyp formation. The Stacking ensemble model serves as a highly accurate tool for identifying individuals at high risk of colorectal polyps, thereby facilitating targeted screening and timely early intervention. These findings support the incorporation of multi-dimensional inflammatory-nutritional biomarkers and machine learning strategies into clinical practice to optimize Colorectal Cancer (CRC) prevention.
